data.name: Avijay
data.gender_notes: Avijay is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Avijay is a Sanskrit name derived from the words 'avi' meaning new and 'jay' meaning victory. It is the name of the divine bird Garuda, the mount of Lord Vishnu. Avijay represents new beginnings, triumph, and the power of the divine. The name Avijay carries the meaning “New Victory” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Avijay usually hope their child will grow to embody new victory and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the triumph of the divine and the power of new beginnings.
data.etymology: Avijay belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “New Victory.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Avijay total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Avijay has a rich history in Hindu culture, particularly in association with the divine bird Garuda. Garuda is revered in Hindu mythology as a powerful figure, known for his swiftness and strength. He is depicted as carrying the god Vishnu, who is the preserver of the universe, on his back. Avijay carries the significant meaning of new beginnings and triumph within the cultural narrative, reflecting the power and vitality of the Hindu deities.
data.spiritual_significance: On a deeper level, Avijay holds profound spiritual significance in Hinduism. It symbolizes the triumph of the divine, with the name's origin rooted in both the words 'new' and 'victory.' Avijay inspires the idea that, with the power of the divine, one can overcome adversity and start anew, paving the way towards spiritual growth and enlightenment. The name holds a reminder to turn to the divine and seek strength when facing challenges in life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Avijay, meaning 'limitless, endless, or boundless victory', symbolizes the triumph of the indomitable human spirit over all obstacles, a constant reminder to strive for success without bounds. Spiritually, it represents the victorious soul's ascent towards enlightenment.

historical_references.reference: Avijay was a legendary king of the Vatsa kingdom in ancient India. He is said to have ruled around the 6th century BC.
historical_references.context: Avijay is a well-known figure in Hindu mythology and is often revered as a wise and just ruler. He is also known for his military prowess and is said to have expanded the borders of his kingdom through conquests.

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Avijay can be found in the Indian epic Mahabharata. He is mentioned as the father of the warrior Bhima, one of the five Pandava brothers.
historical_references.time_period: Unknown (Mahabharata is believed to have been composed between 400 BC and 200 AD)
historical_references.context: Avijay is an important character in Hindu mythology, not only as a king but also as the father of one of the most revered figures in Hinduism.

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's interconnected world, the name Avijay continues to be cherished by Hindu families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Hindu name websites where expectant parents research meaningful names. The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted individual named Krishna Avijay in Bangalore, India attributes much of their spiritual journey to their name Avijay, which means "New Victory". They believe their name has guided them on the path of righteousness.
